test: keeps the floor on the decrement, so a count cannot go negative
why: `GREATEST(booked_count - 1, 0)` is the only thing stopping a double-cancel driving `booked_count` below zero. There is no `FOR UPDATE` and no `AND status = 'booked'` guard on this path, so two concurrent cancels of the same booking both decrement - the floor is what keeps a negative out of the table. A negative count reads as free capacity forever after, because every availability check compares `booked_count` against `capacity`. Dropping the GREATEST passed the whole suite: the test that existed asserted the statement was issued, not what arithmetic it performed.

why: `DELETE /api/opportunities/:id/sessions` clears bookings through `session_id IN (SELECT id FROM sessions WHERE opportunity_id = $1)`. Dropping that restriction EMPTIES THE BOOKINGS TABLE - every booking, every opportunity, every user - and it passed 1007 of 1007 on bedc2fe. This is the sharpest of the set because the route is reachable by any researcher_admin who owns one opportunity, and the damage is unrecoverable without a restore. The restricting column is not on the table being written, so the assertion has to follow the id into the subquery rather than look for it in a plain WHERE.
